- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 day window); apply a 1-2 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- Forecast mean tends to drift higher than true outcome in early horizon (e.g., 1-3 days ahead); apply downward bias adjustment for short-term (1-7 day) forecasts.
- For 10+ day forecasts, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a “pull-back” rule: if forecast > 20% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 10-15%.
- Sentiment volatility > 0.5 in 3-day window correlates with forecast error; use sentiment smoothing (avg of last 3) to dampen erratic forecasts.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings (e.g., +0.8 → -0.5 → +0.6), model tends to misread momentum; apply “sentiment momentum filter” to dampen overconfidence in direction.
